name: Cryptographic Protocols
description: Design and analysis of cryptographic protocols such as TLS, key exchange, messaging, and PKI.
narrative:
At USENIX Security, the cryptographic-protocols thread starts mostly as an empirical, attack-and-measure enterprise focused on the deployed plumbing of the internet. The earliest listed work probes how real PKI and transport security break in practice: "Bamboozling Certificate Authorities with BGP" (2018) shows that BGP hijacks can subvert domain-validated certificate issuance, "The Dangers of Key Reuse: Practical Attacks on IPsec IKE" (2018) revives Bleichenbacher-style oracles against IKE, and "The Broken Shield: Measuring Revocation Effectiveness in the Windows Code-Signing PKI" (2018) measures how poorly revocation actually works. Alongside these, "The Secure Socket API: TLS as an Operating System Service" (2018) reframes the perennial finding that TLS is too hard to use correctly, proposing to move it into the OS.

Over 2019-2021 the work broadens along two axes. One is continued, more systematic attacks and measurement of TLS and its neighbors: "Scalable Scanning and Automatic Classification of TLS Padding Oracle Vulnerabilities" (2019) automates internet-wide vulnerability hunting, while "SHA-1 is a Shambles" (2020) lands the first chosen-prefix collision and breaks the PGP web of trust, a concrete reminder that primitive-level breaks have protocol-level consequences. Email security gets sharp scrutiny too, with "Why TLS is better without STARTTLS" (2021) and "ALPACA" (2021) exposing protocol-confusion and downgrade cracks in how TLS is layered onto application protocols. The second axis is the rise of formal, machine-checked analysis: "A Spectral Analysis of Noise" (2020) gives an automated formal treatment of the whole Noise family of Diffie-Hellman handshakes, signaling a shift from one-off proofs to tool-driven verification.

By 2021-2023 secure messaging and rigorous protocol analysis move to center stage. "The Complexities of Healing in Secure Group Messaging" (2021) studies post-compromise security and cross-group effects in group messaging, and "Three Lessons From Threema" (2023) delivers a full cryptographic teardown of a deployed messenger. Measurement keeps finding sharp edges in TLS internals, as in "We Really Need to Talk About Session Tickets" (2023), which uncovers widespread session-ticket key mismanagement.

Most recently the field turns toward the post-quantum transition and toward TLS as a fingerprinting surface. "Formal verification of the PQXDH Post-Quantum key agreement protocol" (2024) brings machine-checked proofs to Signal's new post-quantum handshake, marking the maturation of formal methods into mainstream protocol design, while "Fingerprinting Obfuscated Proxy Traffic with Encapsulated TLS Handshakes" (2024) shows that even well-built TLS leaks enough metadata to defeat censorship-circumvention proxies. The trajectory runs from cataloguing how deployed crypto breaks, through automated discovery and formal verification, to securing next-generation messaging against quantum and traffic-analysis adversaries.

milestones.title: Bamboozling Certificate Authorities with BGP
milestones.note: showed BGP hijacks can subvert domain-validated certificate issuance, exposing a structural weakness in the web PKI

milestones.title: A Spectral Analysis of Noise: A Comprehensive, Automated, Formal Analysis of Diffie-Hellman Protocols
milestones.note: brought automated formal verification to an entire family of key-exchange handshakes, signaling the shift to tool-driven analysis

milestones.title: SHA-1 is a Shambles: First Chosen-Prefix Collision on SHA-1 and Application to the PGP Web of Trust
milestones.note: delivered the first chosen-prefix SHA-1 collision and broke the PGP web of trust, tying primitive breaks to protocol failure

milestones.title: ALPACA: Application Layer Protocol Confusion - Analyzing and Mitigating Cracks in TLS Authentication
milestones.note: exposed cross-protocol confusion attacks that crack TLS authentication when it is layered onto application protocols

milestones.title: The Complexities of Healing in Secure Group Messaging: Why Cross-Group Effects Matter
milestones.note: advanced the analysis of post-compromise security in group messaging, a defining concern of modern secure messengers

milestones.title: Three Lessons From Threema: Analysis of a Secure Messenger
milestones.note: provided a full cryptographic teardown of a widely deployed encrypted messenger, exemplifying rigorous real-world protocol analysis

milestones.title: Formal verification of the PQXDH Post-Quantum key agreement protocol for end-to-end secure messaging
milestones.note: machine-checked Signal's new post-quantum handshake, marking the field's move into the post-quantum era with formal methods

milestones.title: Fingerprinting Obfuscated Proxy Traffic with Encapsulated TLS Handshakes
milestones.note: showed TLS handshakes leak enough metadata to defeat censorship-circumvention proxies, reframing TLS as a fingerprinting surface
